non-root role managers cannot grant or assign any permission they do not currently hold
non-root administrators cannot mutate built-in global or tenant system roles
every active tenant retains at least one active organization administrator during role and account lifecycle changes
creation and reassignment preserve the exact ordered multi-role set, primary role, and deduplicated effective permission union
every API route is authenticated by a governed identity or integration credential unless present in the bounded public allowlist
the API accepts only explicit production Host values and rejects wildcard trust
the TLS gateway, frontend proxy, and backend use distinct bounded network identities and sanitize forwarded client addresses
refresh rotation is row-locked and replay of a replaced token revokes its full descendant session chain
every user can inspect and revoke only their own sessions with current-session-safe logout behavior
local users can change a policy-compliant password after current-password proof, all sessions are revoked, and external identities remain provider-managed
administrator-issued passwords are temporary, all existing sessions are mandatorily revoked, and server-side access remains restricted until the user changes the password
login input is bounded, unknown identities receive equivalent password-verification work, and rolling email plus sanitized-IP limits use indexed audit windows
policy canary progression and completion require root-attributed metrics evidence, missing or unavailable telemetry fails closed, and metrics destinations cannot be selected by API callers
direct alert execution is root-only and audited, destinations are deployment-fixed, and SMTP, Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook delivery succeeds only after transport confirmation
legacy mock providers and previews are production-disabled, never create confirmed-delivery or imported-record evidence, and remain visibly distinct from the production integration control plane

automation success is reserved for confirmed internal side effects, simulated and skipped actions remain explicit, ticket/rule/runbook/retry execution is tenant isolated, and manual runbooks cannot complete before every governed checklist step

mock email is production-disabled and remains explicit simulation without transport IDs, delivery timestamps, accepted counts, healthy readiness, or retry eligibility; Microsoft Graph acceptance and delivery stay separately evidenced

mock Teams connectors are production-disabled and remain explicit simulation without HTTP status, provider reference, delivery timestamp, attempts, success counters, healthy readiness, or production major-incident routing

local AI simulation and external-provider fallback never claim a live connection or external success; requested/effective provider, model, execution mode, and fallback evidence remain visible across runtime ledgers, APIs, and operator interfaces

custom and multi-role users receive navigation, direct-route access, dashboard requests, metrics, ticket/request visibility scopes, Asset operations, Event Operations, Major Incident access, and actions only from their effective permission union; unscoped record reads fail closed, requester ticket read never implies tenant-wide operational-event access, and denied UI state is explicit while backend authorization remains authoritative

operator consoles distinguish loading, empty, stale, denied, and failed data; failed APIs never appear as valid zero metrics or empty queues, affected sources are identified, and retry remains explicit and accessible
